findings.title: `I18n.ensure_loaded!` is called on the module, but the method is defined on the backend
findings.description: `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` calls `I18n.ensure_loaded! l`. The `ensure_loaded!(locale)` added in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` is indented as an instance method inside the backend class, the same level as `translate`, which calls `load_locale` and `config` on the backend. The hunk does not show a module-level `I18n.ensure_loaded!`. If none exists, `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` raises `NoMethodError`. `application_controller.rb` calls that method on every request that reaches this code, so the failure would hit every page render. The receiver should probably be `I18n.backend.ensure_loaded!`. I could not confirm the class nesting in the patch file, so this needs a check against `translate_accelerator.rb`.

findings.title: Added call changes the return value of the method it sits in
findings.description: The new line `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is added after the `if/else` that ends at line 157, and before the method's closing `end`. Ruby returns the last expression, so the method now returns the result of `ensure_loaded!`, which is the result of `each` (the locale array), not the locale value the `if/else` produced. Any caller that uses this method's return value would receive a different value. I could not read the method's head or its callers, so I could not confirm whether the return value is used. If it is, the side-effect call should move above the value expression or the return should be kept explicit.

findings.title: Verification limited to diff text
findings.description: I had no file-reading or search tools in this session, so I did not read the surrounding code, the method signature in `application_controller.rb`, or the `I18n` backend class nesting in `translate_accelerator.rb`. Both findings above depend on that context and should be checked before they are acted on.
